merger_description:
Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited (**SMTB**) proposes to acquire a minority interest of up to 15% of the units in H.R.L. Morrison & Co Group Limited Partnership (**Morrison LP**) and up to 15% of the ordinary shares in its general partner, H.R.L. Morrison & Co Group GP Limited (**Morrison GP**) (together, **Morrison**) and commit to making investments into two Morrison managed funds (the **Acquisition**).

SMTB is a Japan-based provider of financial services. In Australia, SMTB provides commercial lending services, including general corporate loans, fund financing, and property finance, mainly conducted through offshore booking transactions by SMTB's Singapore Branch, together with minority debt and equity investments in Australian assets and funds. SMTB has a representative office in Sydney, which is focussed only on local market research.

SMTB is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Group, Inc (**SMTG**). SMTG is the holding company of the SMTG corporate group,  a Japanese financial group predominately focused on trust banking and asset management.

Morrison is a global infrastructure investment firm headquartered in New Zealand that invests globally in private and listed infrastructure.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between SMTB and Morrison
in the supply of infrastructure investment and management
services in Australia.
b. the parties’ combined share in the supply of fund
management services to customers in Australia is low, the
increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
would be small and there are alternative suppliers of fund
management services to customers in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
